title: Multi-region edge degradation handoff retrospective
summary: On 2025-11-02 we observed progressive degradation across an edge POP (eu-west-2-edge-3) that manifested as elevated 502/504 rates and increased token latency for a subset of hosted API endpoints. Traffic was automatically weight-shifted toward the warm-standby region (eu-central) via our routing layer and Route53 weighted records. The automatic handoff worked but exposed gaps: our kvcache preseed process was incomplete, causing a spike in cold-cache misses and doubling tail latency for warm-standby replicas. The provider-level route flaps exacerbated control-plane noise and a mis-set autoscaler cooldown prevented timely scale-up of dedicated nodes, contributing to sustained user-impact for ~28 minutes.
incident_timeline: 2025-11-02T09:12Z: First alert — 5xx rate increase from eu-west-2-edge-3 POP (monitoring: api-5xx-rate > 3x baseline)
2025-11-02T09:14Z: SRE on-call paged; quick triage shows BGP adjacencies flapping at edge provider for that POP
2025-11-02T09:17Z: Automated routing policy reduced weight to eu-west primary and shifted ~60% traffic to eu-central warm-standby
2025-11-02T09:18Z: Heatmap shows cache miss rate spike on eu-central replicas (kvcache miss rate +240%)
2025-11-02T09:22Z: Manual increase of weight to eu-central to protect user traffic; however, autoscaler cooldown prevented node spin-up until 09:30Z
2025-11-02T09:30Z: Nodes in eu-central came up, but initial request latency remained elevated due to cold KV loads
2025-11-02T09:40Z: Steady-state restored; routing weights gradually moved back over next 20 minutes as edge POP stabilized
2025-11-02T10:05Z: Post-incident ops call initiated; mitigation actions documented
impact: Approximately 18% of global requests experienced >=2x tail latency for the ~28 minute interval. About 3 enterprise customers reported degraded throughput on integration tests; no data loss. Internal SLIs affected: p95 latency, error-rate SLO burn (short window).
root_cause_analysis: Primary trigger: provider-level BGP instability at a single edge POP causing intermittent egress failures and elevated 502/504 responses. Secondary factors increased customer-visible impact: 1) Warm-standby replicas were not fully warmed (kvcache preseed incomplete), so weight-shift caused large cold-cache pressure; 2) Autoscaler cooldown and min-replica floor configuration prevented fast vertical capacity addition in warm region; 3) DNS TTLs and Route53 propagation were set conservatively, leading to uneven distribution during automated weights change. Additionally, our healthcheck aggregation window hid early signs of degradation because a minority of POPs were failing but cluster-level aggregation threshold was not sensitive enough.
mitigations: Immediate: Manually adjust Route53 weights to move traffic away from affected POP while preserving session affinity for critical customers
Immediate: Triggered ad-hoc kvcache preseed job to prime hot keys in eu-central (short-term fix)
Short-term: Lowered autoscaler cooldown and adjusted min-replica floor for warm-standby to allow faster scale-up during handoffs
Long-term: Work with edge provider to get BGP adjacencies stabilized and demand better incident transparency
runbook_draft: Objective: provide a concise, operator-friendly series of steps for a region-level edge degradation that requires shifting traffic to warm-standby. Preconditions: warm-standby region health checks passing (healthcheck >= 99.5%), kvcache seeds available, runbook IAM role. Steps: 1) Confirm degradation is localized to a POP/region (check edge-pop-5xx metric by POP). 2) Validate warm-standby readyness: check kvcache hit-rate, node CPU, disk I/O, and 'warm-standby-ready' tag on instances. 3) If automatic route weight policy triggers, monitor kvcache miss rate in warm region; if miss rate > 150% baseline, trigger preseed. 4) Run kvcache preseed: trigger job id 'preseed-<timestamp>' and monitor unfinished keys; wait until hot key miss rate falls below threshold. 5) Adjust DNS/route weights gradually: test 10% increments every 2 minutes and verify p95/p99 latency and error-rate signals. 6) If latency remains elevated after 3 increments, pause and scale up replicas manually. 7) Once steady-state achieved, document exact weights and times and notify CS for customer comms. 8) Post-incident: run the kvcache integrity check and create follow-up tickets for any keys that failed to preseed. Notes: prefer weight adjustments over single-step failovers, keep DNS TTL at 30s for critical records during incident windows, snapshot kv seeds before drastic traffic shifts.
playbook_commands:
# check POP-level 5xx by POP
kubectl --context=prod exec -it deploy/edge-metrics -- curl -s http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query?query=pop_5xx_rate

# manual Route53 weighted change (example)
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes": [{"Action": "UPSERT", "ResourceRecordSet": {"Name": "api.redwood.ai", "Type": "A", "SetIdentifier": "eu-central-weight", "Weight": 700, "TTL": 30, "ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "203.0.113.10"}]}}]}'

# trigger kvcache preseed job
./ops/bin/preseed_kvcache --region eu-central --job-id preseed-$(date +%s)

# check preseed progress
kubectl -n infra logs job/preseed-<id> --follow

# scale replica set in warm region
kubectl --context=eu-central scale rs/api-serving --replicas=8

# quick healthcheck to a sample host
curl -v https://eu-central-api-1.redwood.ai/health | jq .status

retrospective_notes: Key takeaway: automated routing policies do the right thing by protecting customers quickly, but they surface downstream capacity and cache priming issues that produce secondary user-visible pain. We should move from reactive to proactive: automated preseed + conservative ramping + improved pop-level sensitivity in alerts. Communication: improve CS templating for short-duration latency incidents so customers see consistent messaging. Also revise SRE on-call runbooks to emphasize pre-checks for warm-standby readiness before increasing weight beyond a small step.
